description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Join an engineering team developing robots for real-world service environments. You will work across hardware integration and teleoperation software to identify and remove the barriers that keep robots from reliably completing complex maintenance tasks.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Assess robot capabilities and identify hardware and software constraints in service bays.

 - Build, test, and improve teleoperation rigs on real maintenance tasks.

 - Integrate robot arms, end effectors, cameras, and VR or leader-follower control systems.

 - Break complex repairs into testable subtasks, including accessing fasteners, disconnecting hoses, and manipulating tools in confined spaces.

 - Diagnose failures across visibility, latency, perception, motion control, reach, and dexterity.

 - Test whether force feedback, force/torque sensing, compliant control, or improved tooling can resolve task bottlenecks.

 - Track completion rates, cycle times, and operator interventions, and collect synchronized robot and sensor data for policy learning.

 - Move validated tasks from bench experiments to supervised trials in live service bays.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Hands-on experience building and debugging physical robots.

 - A strong background in robotic manipulation or teleoperation.

 - Proficiency in C++, Python, and ROS 2 or equivalent frameworks.

 - Experience designing experiments that distinguish software limitations from hardware constraints.

 - A rigorous approach to safety when operating robots around people and vehicles.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Base salary range: $205,000 to $305,000 annually. Visa sponsorship is not available.


LOCATION

On-site in San Francisco, California, United States.
